title: Great Fire of London
summary: The Great Fire of London began in the King's baker's house on Pudding Lane in the City of London on 2 September 1666. Over four days, the University of Oxford's Faculty of History says, it destroyed about 85 percent of the area within the city walls, wiping out 13,200 houses and 86 parish churches and leaving 70,000 to 80,000 people homeless. By 13 September the king had set the aim of rebuilding in brick or stone and proposed street widening.
